newsitem.title: HUNGARY: EU seeks more active Mideast role - Spring.
newsitem.headline: EU seeks more active Mideast role - Spring.

text.p: Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring said on Sunday that the European Union strongly favoured playing a bigger part in Middle East peace diplomacy.

"There's a very strong feeling within the European Union that we should play a more active role in relation to discussions taking place between the Israelis and the Palestinians," Spring, whose country holds the rotating EU presidency, said during a visit to Hungary.

Spring, who recently returned from a fact-finding tour of the Middle East, spoke on the eve of a meeting of the EU's General Affairs Council in Luxembourg which will consider appointing a special Middle East envoy.
His comments appeared to put him on the side of France and others within the EU who favour a more active European effort to try to revive the virtually collapsed peace process in the Middle East.
French President Jacques Chirac toured the Middle East this month with the avowed aim of making Europe a co-sponsor with the United States of Arab-Israeli talks.
Spring said he had spoken several times to U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher about the proposal to name a European envoy to the Middle East.
He said there was no intention by the EU to try to supplant the work of U.S. Middle East peace negotiator Dennis Ross.

"We are the main financial donor of aid to the region and we are also the main trading partner of most countries in the region, including Israel," he told a joint news conference after meeting Hungarian Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs.
"We are presently discussing the question of appointing a special envoy to represent the European Union and that will be discussed in fact in Luxembourg tomorrow."
Kovacs and Spring said they discussed Hungary's bid to join the EU, which Spring said Ireland fully supported, and also an expanded role for Hungary in peacekeeping forces.

"The peacekeeping record of Hungary is much shorter...than that of Ireland. In Cyprus we have a small unit of 40 soldiers doing some peacekeeping work and we also have some limited units of peacekeepers in the Sinai," Kovacs said.
"What we need is more experience and that is the reason I raised the exchange of experience with the minister because we want to benefit from the experience of Ireland."
